stories.body: A 16-year-old killed three children aged five, eight and 11, and a teacher after forcing his way into Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, police said. A seven-year-old pupil and a 54-year-old teacher were critically injured. Police said the attacker fired at locked doors to enter the school and was then pursued and fatally shot by a community member before officers arrived. Investigators have not said whether he had a connection to the school.
stories.headline: Four killed, including three children, in Oregon primary school shooting

stories.body: Ukraine said it would resume attacks on Russian oil refineries after a brief pause intended to support a proposed US-brokered energy ceasefire. Russia accused Ukraine of attacking a refinery in the Ryazan region, while Ukraine said Russia continued striking its energy infrastructure and launched hundreds of drones against central regions. Zelenskyy also said US restrictions on intelligence sharing and satellite services were limiting Ukraine's defence, as European leaders voiced concern over reduced US support. Separately, a drone attack set a chemical tanker on fire near Romania, leaving sailors missing.
stories.headline: Ukraine resumes refinery strikes as Trump-backed energy ceasefire collapses

stories.body: At least five people were killed and 16 wounded when Houthi forces attacked the presidential palace complex in Aden, the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government. The government said missiles and drones were used, while the Houthis said they had targeted Saudi military operations in the city. Yemen's prime minister and cabinet members were reported safe. The strike came amid an escalation between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition, including repeated attacks on Saudi infrastructure and threats to regional shipping and aviation.
stories.headline: Houthi missile and drone attack on Yemen government palace kills five

stories.body: Israel said commercial shipments had not entered Gaza for two days, blaming a dispute over fees and payment demands that it attributes to Hamas. Gaza authorities and the territory's truckers rejected that account, saying Israeli restrictions were responsible. The halt affects goods such as fruit and winter clothing and threatens a key source of supplies for Gaza's 2.1 million residents, where aid agencies say humanitarian deliveries alone cannot meet demand or keep prices stable. Gaza health officials also reported that hospitals were under severe pressure as critically ill patients were unable to leave the territory.
stories.headline: Israel halts commercial goods entering Gaza, as hospitals report severe pressure

stories.body: France and Germany have reached a preliminary agreement to soften aspects of EU car-emissions policy while strengthening European sourcing rules for the automotive industry. The reported deal would preserve the target for a 90% reduction in combustion-engine CO2 emissions by 2035, but remove a requirement to compensate for the remaining emissions, citing the growing use of sustainable fuels. It would also favour components made in Europe, Britain and Norway, an effort to protect European manufacturers and suppliers amid increased competition from Chinese carmakers.
stories.headline: France and Germany back looser EU car-emissions rules and a 'made in Europe' plan

stories.body: Former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, pleaded not guilty in New York to new US charges alleging a state-sponsored campaign of torture. Prosecutors allege that the pair oversaw or helped develop a system that used beatings, electric shocks, asphyxiation, sexual violence, isolation, starvation and psychological abuse against opponents, including US citizens. Maduro called the allegations false, and both defendants continue to argue that their former positions give them sovereign immunity. They have been held in New York since their capture by US forces in January, and their trial is scheduled for June 2027.
stories.headline: Maduro and his wife plead not guilty to new US torture charges

stories.body: Democratic Senate candidates substantially outraised many Republican rivals in third-quarter filings across key races, including Texas, Georgia, North Carolina, Michigan, Maine, Ohio, Iowa, Alaska, New Hampshire and Kansas. Politico reported that the Democratic candidates in those ten contests collectively raised more than five times as much as their Republican opponents. Republicans retain advantages in some campaign cash balances and outside-group support, including funding linked to Elon Musk and MAGA Inc., but the candidate-level gaps could matter because campaigns receive lower television advertising rates.
stories.headline: Democratic Senate candidates open major fundraising leads over Republican rivals

stories.body: Donald Trump blamed Republican strategist Karl Rove and former senator John Cornyn for making it harder for Texas attorney general Ken Paxton, Trump's preferred candidate, to defeat Democratic state lawmaker James Talarico in the Senate race. Recent polling has shown a tight contest in a state Trump won comfortably in 2024. Talarico reported a record-breaking $64 million third-quarter fundraising haul, while national Republican groups have committed large sums to support Paxton and attack his opponent.
stories.headline: Trump attacks fellow Republicans as Ken Paxton struggles in Texas Senate race

stories.body: Two unnamed women have sued former Florida congressman Matt Gaetz, former Seminole County tax collector Joel Greenberg and former state legislator Chris Dorworth in federal court, alleging a sex-trafficking scheme that exploited their financial vulnerability. The civil lawsuit echoes allegations examined by the House Ethics Committee, including claims involving payments, drugs, travel and commercial sex acts. Gaetz denied the allegations and said he would contest them. Greenberg is serving an 11-year federal sentence after pleading guilty to offences including sex trafficking of a minor and wire fraud; the Justice Department previously closed its investigation of Gaetz without bringing charges.
stories.headline: Two women file sex-trafficking lawsuit against former congressman Matt Gaetz

stories.body: Spain's Central Electoral Board has opened a sanction proceeding against Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez over an October 6 press conference at Moncloa Palace, held after snap elections were called for November 29. The board said Sánchez may have gone beyond explaining government housing decrees by criticising the opposition, promoting his government's record and calling for a broader parliamentary majority. It ordered the removal of the disputed statements from official channels and reminded him of his duty of political neutrality during the electoral period. A finding against him could lead to a fine.
stories.headline: Spain's electoral board opens another case against Sánchez over campaigning from Moncloa

stories.body: Spain's National Intelligence Centre has submitted its report to National Court judge María Tardón as she investigates the mass entry of about 80,000 people into Ceuta on July 30. The judge has requested information from 21 police, military and intelligence bodies to establish who coordinated, financed and decided the operation. The inquiry has not yet named suspects, and much of the requested information remains outstanding.
stories.headline: Spain's intelligence service submits report on mass entry into Ceuta to investigating judge

stories.body: Spain's Defence Ministry has sent to a Ceuta court and prosecutors recordings in which soldiers allegedly describe and mock assaults on migrants. The ministry said it was cooperating with the investigation of possible crimes to protect the armed forces' reputation. The reported recordings include accounts of beatings and humiliating treatment, including an alleged episode in which one migrant was forced to assault others. Amnesty International said the alleged conduct could amount to torture or cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment. Defence is also investigating legionnaires who appeared in a video cheering far-right agitator Vito Quiles.
stories.headline: Defence ministry refers recordings of soldiers mocking assaults on migrants in Ceuta to justice authorities

stories.body: Chilean writer Isabel Allende has won the 75th Premio Planeta, worth €1 million, for La hora antes del alba. The novel is a sequel to her first book, La casa de los espíritus, and returns to the story of Alba, who comes back to her family home pregnant after suffering imprisonment, torture and rape during Chile's dictatorship. Allende said she had returned to that world because of her concern about democracies threatened by nationalism and fascism. Valencian writer and screenwriter Sergio Hernández was runner-up with La añoranza.
stories.headline: Isabel Allende wins the 75th Premio Planeta for 'La hora antes del alba'

stories.body: Catalonia's Civil Protection agency has activated the Inuncat alert plan for intense rain expected from Saturday afternoon into early Sunday. Meteocat has issued high-risk warnings for nine counties, including Osona, La Selva, Vallès Oriental, Vallès Occidental, Barcelonès, Baix Llobregat and Garraf, with possible rainfall above 20 litres per square metre in 30 minutes and 60 litres in three hours. Storms may bring hail and local flooding. Authorities advise people to follow official updates, check travel conditions and avoid rivers, streams and other flood-prone areas.
stories.headline: Catalan authorities issue fresh heavy-rain warnings for Saturday

stories.body: The UGT union has begun conciliation proceedings to require the 365 chain to apply the hospitality-sector agreement to 790 workers in its Barcelona-area cafés instead of the bakery agreement. UGT says the cafés provide tables, seating and terraces, serve food and drinks for consumption on site, and employ staff to prepare and serve food, assist customers and take payment. It argues that the lower-paid bakery agreement does not reflect the businesses' main activity and should not be used to reduce labour costs. The request does not cover workers at the chain's central bakery.
stories.headline: UGT demands that Barcelona's 365 café chain apply the hospitality labour agreement

stories.body: Ateneu del Clot says it still lacks clear information about its planned move to the municipally owned Fàbrica del Plom, despite a temporary five-year lease at its current premises secured after neighbourhood mobilisation. The association wants a timetable for the factory's rehabilitation and clarity on how it would coexist with the neighbourhood centre planned for the same site. Barcelona City Council says the project is continuing and that more details will be available after approval, with works expected to be tendered during the next term. The Ateneu fears its current lease will end before the new facility is ready.
stories.headline: Barcelona's Ateneu del Clot warns of uncertainty over its promised move to the Fàbrica del Plom
